steps.title: Research hub — new 3-way lab tile
steps.narration: The Research hub now shows a brand-new tile for the Regime × Phase × Factor lab, sitting alongside the existing Regime Lab and Phase & Severity Lab. Two clicks from the Research nav entry in the sidebar is all it takes to reach the full lab.
steps.point_out: The 'Regime × Phase × Factor' tile in the LABS grid, with its Boxes icon and one-line description beneath it.

steps.title: Enter the 3-way combination lab
steps.narration: Clicking the tile opens the Regime × Phase × Factor lab — a factor selector at the top, three decile filter dropdowns, and a ranked combination table with paired forward-return and max-drawdown columns at every horizon for each regime × severity × factor triple.
steps.point_out: The factor selector defaulting to Leadership Score, the three filter dropdowns each showing All, and the pagination footer reading 'Page 1 of 16' — the combination data has loaded.

steps.title: Switch the factor — table re-renders with new data
steps.narration: Selecting Entry Quality Score from the factor dropdown triggers a fresh fetch and re-renders the entire combination table using that factor's decile boundaries. The n values and row rankings are completely different from the Leadership Score view.
steps.point_out: The selected option now reads 'Entry Quality score' and the table rows have changed — a new ranking of (regime, severity, factor) combinations appears at the top of the first page.

steps.title: Filter to regime decile D10 — instant client-side narrowing
steps.narration: Selecting D10 in the Regime Decile filter instantly removes every row from any lower regime decile. This is a pure client-side view transform — no API call, no loading spinner — so the result is immediate.
steps.point_out: Every visible row now shows D10 in the Regime D column. The visible row count has dropped and only the highest-regime-score combinations are displayed.

steps.title: Sort by forward return — NA combinations stay at the bottom
steps.narration: Clicking a column header sorts the visible rows in either direction. Combinations with too few qualifying samples show NA and are pinned to the bottom regardless of sort direction, so the evidence-backed rows always float to the top.
steps.point_out: The D10 regime rows are now ordered by 1-day forward return. Page 1 shows only numeric-valued rows — any NA combinations have been pushed to the later pages.

steps.title: Open the lab with a historical date ready
steps.narration: The product shares a single global date control across all research pages. Loading the lab with a May 2024 date in the URL sets that shared control, so one click on the toggle switches the entire combination table to historical-window mode.
steps.point_out: The combination table in All-history mode, showing the full observation window with 'Page 1 of 16'. Note the n values in the first few rows before the point-in-time filter is applied.

steps.title: Activate As-of date — n values shrink to the historical window
steps.narration: Clicking 'As of date' restricts every combination's sample pool to scanner snapshots dated up to May 31 2024. The n values immediately drop and the page count falls from 16 to 14 — only the evidence that actually existed at that historical date is counted.
steps.point_out: 'Point-in-time: pooling only snapshots dated ≤ 2024-05-31' is visible in the banner. The n values for the top rows are noticeably smaller than in All-history mode, and pagination now shows Page 1 of 14.

steps.title: Drill through an N= chip to the exact observation cohort
steps.narration: Every n= chip in the combination table links to a Research Samples view pre-filtered to that exact (regime, severity, factor, horizon) cohort. The Total observations count on the Samples page matches the chip number precisely — the same single data source, no rounding.
steps.point_out: The Research Samples page shows 'Total observations: 338', matching the chip clicked from the Leadership score / Regime D7 × Severity D5 × Factor D10 / 1-day combination. The cohort description names every dimension clearly.
